solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Handicap: Velia's deep in trouble

parts.note: Velia is the setter, so 'Velia's' stands for 'I am', shortened to I'M

indicators.note: letters in trouble are thrown into disorder, so the word deep is rearranged

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to being in a mess, which is a handicap.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name, so 'Velia's' is 'Velia is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To handicap someone is to hinder or obstruct them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Pagan vows in future

parts.note: the wedding vows are the words 'I do'
in future means later, at some time to come

explanation.surface: A heathen swearing oaths about what is to come.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagan worships idols rather than the god of the main religions, so is an idol-worshipper.

clue.text: Royal home counties first to get media coverage

indicators.note: media coverage here means the press wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: the press is the news media
at home is 'in'

indicators.note: first says only the opening letter of counties is used

explanation.surface: A royal visit to the Home Counties near London gets the newspapers' attention first.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London; 'home' is a separate piece here.
explanation.definitionFit: A princess is a female member of a royal family, so a royal by example.

clue.text: Doctor extremely understanding, sure to reform addict

indicators.note: extremely takes only the extreme letters, first and last, of understanding
to reform is to re-form, so the letters of sure are reshaped

explanation.surface: A sympathetic doctor is sure an addict can reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes UG from 'understanding'; 'to reform' rearranges SURE into USER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dependent on narcotics is an addict, the plain sense of this phrase.

clue.text: Come together when disorder returns with capacity to contain it

indicators.note: to contain says the capacity word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: having the capacity to do something is being able

indicators.note: returns means the word for disorder is read backwards

parts.note: a mess is a state of disorder

explanation.surface: People gather when chaos breaks out again, as long as there is room to hold it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' simply points back to the reversed disorder that the capacity word holds.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble is to gather or meet up, a direct synonym of coming together.

clue.text: Rob disrupting grandma's bash!

indicators.note: disrupting throws the letters of grandma's bash into a new order

explanation.surface: A robbery ruins a grandmother's party.
explanation.definitionFit: A smash-and-grab is a raid where a shop window is broken and goods snatched, a kind of robbery.

clue.text: Tired out west gun-toting literary style

indicators.note: toting means carrying, so the shortened word holds the gun inside it
out says the letter for west is dropped from the word for tired

parts.note: weary means tired
W is the compass abbreviation for west
a pistol is a handgun

explanation.surface: A weary gunslinger out in the Wild West, described in some literary style.
explanation.walkthrough: WEARY loses W ('out west') to leave EARY, which carries PISTOL ('toting') to make E-PISTOL-ARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Epistolary writing is told through letters, a recognised literary form such as the letter novel.

clue.text: Sweepers in second rate digs?

parts.note: something second-rate is B grade, so B
digs is British slang for rented lodgings, rooms

explanation.surface: Cleaners working in shabby lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digs' is British slang for rented rooms, especially students'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brooms are tools for sweeping floors, so they are sweepers.

clue.text: Make beloved say, "what comes after M darling?"

indicators.note: say tells us the letter is spelt as it is spoken, the name of the letter

parts.note: the letter after M in the alphabet is N
dear is a term of endearment like darling

explanation.surface: A child asks a loved one about the alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' asks for the name of the letter after M, written out as EN.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to cause someone to be loved or liked, so to make them beloved.

clue.text: Old, into undies — extremely disgusting!

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters, first and last, of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Old underwear being worn is revolting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks attached to 'disgusting', but it works on the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious means hateful or repulsive, a close synonym of disgusting.

clue.text: Rubber gloves ruin one medal

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin
I is the Roman numeral one
gold is the top medal

explanation.surface: A pair of rubber gloves spoils a winner's medal.
explanation.walkthrough: Marigold is a well-known British brand of household rubber gloves.
explanation.definitionFit: Marigolds is the trade name used in Britain for yellow rubber washing-up gloves.

clue.text: Targeting aid is right during awfully cruel battle

indicators.note: during says one piece sits in the middle of the other
awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters of cruel battle are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something helps a gunner aim during a dreadful fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracer round leaves a visible trail so a gunner can correct their aim, an aid to targeting.

clue.text: Knowing to take the first of the month off

indicators.note: taking away the first of the month leaves the word without its opening letter
off signals that a letter is removed from the month's name

parts.note: the month here is March

explanation.surface: Being wise enough to have the first day of the month as a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch look or remark is knowing, slyly playful, a common adjectival sense.

clue.text: Beat in song producing heart trouble

indicators.note: in puts the beat word inside the song word

parts.note: an aria is an operatic song
a beat is a rhythm

explanation.surface: A singer's rhythm causes cardiac problems.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrhythmia is an irregular heartbeat, a medical condition of the heart.

clue.text: Box of novelties I distributed

indicators.note: distributed spreads the letters of the words about into a new order

explanation.surface: A container holding novelty items handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' is British slang for the TV set.
explanation.definitionFit: The box is informal British slang for the TV set.

clue.text: Royal following orient light is a christian symbol

indicators.note: following places the royal piece after the eastern piece

parts.note: the Orient is the East
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch
a candle is a light

explanation.surface: A royal comes after an eastern light, suggesting religious imagery.
explanation.definitionFit: The paschal candle lit at the Easter vigil represents the risen Christ in church ritual.

clue.text: Harsh dirt's dished up on hospital department

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, dirt plus S
ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department

explanation.surface: Muck served on a hospital ward is a scathing complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice or tone is loud and grating, so harsh.

clue.text: Is racist out of control in this period?

indicators.note: out of control signals the letters of is racist run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about whether bigotry ran rife in a past era.
explanation.definitionFit: The Triassic is a geological period, the first of the Mesozoic era, when dinosaurs appeared.

clue.text: Arbitrator set up a retro-style appliance

parts.note: a ref, referee, arbitrates in sport
to rig is to set up equipment

indicators.note: style here means the letters of a retro are fashioned anew

explanation.surface: A referee installs a vintage-look kitchen fridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrigerator is a household appliance for keeping food cold.

clue.text: Series of unfortunate events spread on board

indicators.note: on board means within the ship letters, so the spread goes inside them

parts.note: on board means aboard a ship, and SS stands for steamship
pâté is a spread for toast

explanation.surface: A run of bad luck, nodding to the Lemony Snicket books, as something is smeared across a board.
explanation.definitionFit: Spates are sudden floods or rushes of things, often unwelcome, coming in quick succession.

clue.text: Some kir on ice with a twist 2

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A chilled French aperitif served with a twist of peel.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray '2' at the end appears to be a typo in the published clue. Kir is a drink of white wine and blackcurrant liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with a twist has an unexpected wry turn, which is what ironic outcomes have.

clue.text: Special role is coming up — likely audition required at the start

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

indicators.note: at the start takes the opening letter of each of the six words

explanation.surface: An actor hears of a special role, with an audition needed first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the start' looks attached to 'required', but it picks the first letters of the six words before it, ICULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Particular means specific or out of the ordinary, as in particular care, a synonym of special.

clue.text: Greeting sounding more cheerful

indicators.note: sounding says the word for more cheerful is heard, not spelt

parts.note: higher spirits are more cheerful ones

explanation.surface: A hello that comes across as happier.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiya is an informal hello, a casual salutation.

clue.text: See 3
Substantial returns in brown fields firms up stuff of value

indicators.note: in puts the reversed piece inside the brown fields

parts.note: tan is a light brown
leas are meadows or fields, a poetic word

indicators.note: returns means the word for substantial is read backwards

parts.note: something substantial is big
jelly sets when it firms up

explanation.surface: Profits from developed land strengthen the valuables, in a financial report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' makes GIB, which goes 'in' TAN + LEAS; 'Substantial' looks like the definition but is the reversed piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical property such as buildings and machinery is booked as tangible assets, things of value one can touch.

clue.text: See 24
Thus token arrangement needed for time off

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quoted error

indicators.note: arrangement means the letters of token are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An arranged token is all you need to get a day off.
explanation.walkthrough: A sick note is a British term for a doctor's note excusing absence from work or school.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's certificate excusing work stands by metonymy for the absence it allows.

clue.text: Freezing a Roman Catholic movement

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary movement

explanation.surface: A Catholic movement in a chilly climate.
explanation.definitionFit: Arctic weather is bitterly cold, so the word is used for freezing conditions.
